title: BlindToChange: AI Agents Can Find Changes When Asked But Do They Look When Needed?
title_zh: BlindToChange：AI智能体被问到时能发现变化，但需要时会主动查看吗？

paragraphs.en: 提出BlindToChange基准，揭示AI智能体在未被明确提示时难以主动发现影响回答的近期世界事件。 Given that AI agents can search the web broadly and deeply in real time, it is tempting to conclude that their outputs account for recent world events. We show that this conclusion does not hold in practice. While agents can search and easily find recent changes, the correctness of their responses depends on whether they search and what they search for. Popular agentic search benchmarks like BrowseComp cannot expose failures wherein agents do not recognize their own assumptions that should be verified, since these benchmarks explicitly state what needs to be found. In contrast, many user requests state only the final information need (e.g., an itinerary for a trip), leaving the agent to discover relevant changes (e.g., the temporary closure of a museum) and account for their consequences. To highlight such gaps, we introduce BlindToChange, a benchmark that measures whether agents proactively discover recent events that affect their responses. Our benchmark comprises requests for recommendations where an obvious candidate is no longer applicable due to a recent real-world event. These events are drawn automatically from Wikidata, allowing BlindToChange to be periodically refreshed. Strikingly, we find a big gap -- as high as 27.5 points, even at high reasoning effort -- in systems' performance, when the recent event is not explicitly mentioned compared to when we ask about it directly. Analyzing search trajectories, we learn that more than half of the failures can be attributed to the fact that agents do not directly search to verify whether a relevant fact has changed. Our benchmark highlights, and tracks, a new axis of progress, wherein systems account for recent information that is not explicitly mentioned in the user request.
paragraphs.zh: 提出BlindToChange基准，揭示智能体在未被明确提示时难以主动发现影响回答的近期世界事件。鉴于智能体可以实时广泛而深入地搜索网络，人们很容易认为其输出已经考虑了近期的世界事件。 我们表明，这一结论在实践中并不成立。 虽然智能体能够搜索并轻松找到近期变化，但其回答的正确性取决于它们是否进行了搜索以及搜索了什么内容。 像BrowseComp这样流行的智能体搜索基准无法暴露智能体未能识别自身应加验证的假设这类失败，因为这些基准明确说明了需要查找的内容。 相比之下，许多用户请求只陈述最终的信息需求（例如，一次旅行的行程安排），而需要智能体自行发现相关的变化（例如，某家博物馆临时闭馆）并考虑其影响。 为了凸显这类缺口，我们提出了BlindToChange，这是一个衡量智能体能否主动发现影响其回答的近期事件的基准。 我们的基准由推荐类请求组成，其中某个显而易见的候选选项因近期真实世界事件而不再适用。 这些事件自动取自Wikidata，使BlindToChange能够定期更新。 令人惊讶的是，我们发现存在巨大差距——即使在高推理强度下也高达27.5分——当近期事件未被明确提及时，系统的表现明显低于我们直接询问该事件时的表现。 通过分析搜索轨迹，我们发现超过一半的失败可归因于智能体没有直接搜索以验证相关事实是否已经发生变化。 我们的基准凸显并追踪了一条新的进展维度：系统能够考虑用户请求中未明确提及的近期信息。
